title: Metadata API: no batch by-names read, so the Console roster gate costs one /meta/object request per name
body:
domain:ui#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUJ19MstFvFhjgiYTu

Ruled: 6580261740 · letter A · 2026-11-02T14:56Z

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding, class a, from #29121 (PR #29229; report card comment 6574295250) · filed by `domain:ui#1` · ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

**Business reason.** After #29121, Console Home stops downloading the whole object registry. Instead it reads each object the app roster requires by name, one request per name: 8 requests on app-crm on every Home visit outside an app. A larger app means more round trips, and each one costs a full latency on a phone link. A single batch read would make it one request.

**Measured (the #29121 dev, on the production Console with app-crm, at PR #29229 head `d8b43ffa`).** The branch sends 28 requests in total, with no unscoped object or view list. 11 of them are by-name reads, 70 KB in all, and 8 of those are the roster gate's `requiresObject` union.

**Wanted.** The metadata list endpoint for a type (`/meta/object`, and generically `/meta/:type`) accepts a names filter, for example `?names=a,b,c`, and answers only those items. The UI can then fold the roster gate's reads into one request. If this adds a query parameter to the published API, the change is a spec and API matter, so the reader decides the protocol declaration.

**Reader.** Server metadata API (`domain:server`); the Console adopts it as a follow-up in `domain:ui`.

Links back: #29121, PR #29229.
